newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan says MPs pledge to oppose Yilmaz.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan says MPs pledge to oppose Yilmaz.

text.p: Turkey's caretaker prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan, said on Wednesday he possessed signed guarantees that a majority of MPs would reject a secularist coalition to keep his Islamists out of power.

"A total of 278 deputies have signed up to reject a (Mesut) Yilmaz government," Erbakan told a news conference. He produced what he said was a petition of signatures from MPs against plans for a coalition under opposition leader Yilmaz.
Yilmaz, appointed by the president last week to form a government, is just short of the majority needed to win a confidence vote in the 550-seat parliament.
He has won the backing of secularist MPs from the left and right but will rely on support from dissidents in the rival conservative True Path Party, whose leader Tansu Ciller is allied with Erbakan.
Yilmaz has given himself until early next week to present President Suleyman Demirel a government list to replace Erbakan's one-year-old government.
Erbakan resigned last week to resolve a growing dispute with the military over religious activism. He has proposed a revamped coalition of his Islamists and the True Path under Ciller's leadership.
He criticised the president for appointing Yilmaz as prime minister-designate without taking into account the fact that the pro-Islamic alliance has more deputies.
"This is a parliamentiary majority. It binds everyone, it binds the president," said Erbakan waving his piece of paper. He said he would present the signatures to Demirel.
